notes.groups: Seat groups for the limper, squeeze, limp-raise and 4-bet spots: EP (first seats), MP (middle), CO, BTN, SB, BB. More players behind = tighter.
notes.vsLimpers: raise = iso-raise, limp = overlimp (complete from the SB), anything else folds (the big blind checks). Iso-raise hands that play well heads-up with the initiative and dominate limping ranges: pairs, strong broadways, strong suited aces. Overlimp hands that want a cheap multi-way flop: small pairs (sets), suited connectors and suited aces (nut draws), especially late and with more limpers. Fold offsuit hands that flop weak one-pair hands multi-way (KTo, QJo from early seats). The iso range gets tighter as limpers increase (key 3 = 3 or more limpers). Casino 100bb: deeper stacks make overlimping small pairs and suited connectors more attractive (implied odds). Iso size 3bb + 1bb per limper.
notes.squeeze: An open plus callers before you. Squeeze sizes come from sizing.ts (about 3x the open + 1 open per caller in position, 4x + 1 per caller out of position). Calls favour hands that play well multi-way.
notes.vsLimpRaise: You limped and someone raised behind. Limping ranges contain few strong hands, so most limps fold; the calls are hands that play well in a multi-way pot. This spot mostly teaches that limp-calling is weak.
notes.vs4bet: You 3-bet and face a 4-bet. 5bet = all-in. At 100bb some strong hands flat the 4-bet in position; A5s/A4s 5-bet as bluffs part of the time (@50).
